## Two more worth posting

**POST 2**

> freight fraud has a weird zero-trust problem.
>
> if somebody steals the real shipment details, checking the truck against those shipment details proves surprisingly little.
>
> “does the information match?” and “is this actually the authorized person/equipment?” are very different questions.

The Virginia case is unusually good evidence for this distinction. According to the post summarizing the indictment, the thieves allegedly used actual carrier information and actual shipment information, so superficial matching controls behaved exactly as designed and still produced the wrong answer. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="11"}

**POST 3**

> starting to think “autonomous trucking” undersells the infrastructure change.
>
> roads, weigh stations, gates, yards + docks were all designed assuming a human could explain what the truck was doing.
>
> now the infrastructure has to understand the truck directly.
>
> that seems... consequential.

This one is deliberately a question disguised as an observation. PrePass/Kodiak is evidence that the transition has already begun, but don't leap from one integration to “every facility must immediately support autonomous trucks.” :chatgpt-content-reference{index="12"}
